title: Navigation-assisted transoral endoscopic surgery for mandibular ramus–condyle tumours
html: Neoplasms of the mandibular ascending ramus and condyle cause facial asymmetry, trismus, malocclusion, swelling in the temporomandibular joint area, and pain. Conventional surgeries require an external incision, with a risk of facial nerve injury and leaving a scar. This study aimed to establish a minimally invasive approach for mandibular ramus–condyle tumour resection, using intraoperative navigation and endoscopes. The safety and feasibility were assessed by cadaveric dissection. Nine patients with osteomas or osteochondromas occurring from the mandibular ascending ramus and condyle were included in this study.
